method.selection: Healthcare: minimum total current cost within the selected healthy-year gap of the best observed outcome worldwide. Other categories: minimum public cost meeting outcome quantiles. Linear population scaling.
method.scope: Ten disjoint COFOG public-spending categories, all levels of government. Non-health references: 30 European countries. Healthcare selection: global current-cost comparisons, with a separately sourced COFOG public budget.
assumptions: Reference systems can be transferred and combined.
method.outcomeInterpretation: Observed reference outcomes, not predicted combined gains. HALE is a population average, not median healthspan.
method.ranges: Up to three cheapest qualifying alternatives per category; not confidence intervals.

policies.name: Universal insurance with a shared price schedule
policies.description: Public insurance covers the population. A national fee schedule sets reimbursement prices across insurance plans and providers.
policies.periodNote: Universal insurance dates to 1961; this ministry-hosted account predates the 2017–2019 comparison.

policies.name: Income-based limits on large medical bills
policies.description: High-cost medical benefits cap household copayments according to income and age, with extra protection for repeated expensive treatment.
policies.periodNote: Described in the 2019 ministry report; its insurance-system table is dated April 2020. No current thresholds are assumed.

policies.name: Payments that encourage generic medicines
policies.description: The 2018 fee revision rewarded prescriptions using generic names and discouraged pharmacies with very low generic substitution.
policies.periodNote: The 2018 revision occurred during the comparison period; its separate effect on national outcomes is not estimated.

policies.name: One national insurance pool
policies.description: National Health Insurance combines employment and regional insurance in one insurer, pooling contributions and purchasing covered care nationally.
policies.periodNote: Insurers merged in 2000; employment and regional finances were integrated in 2003.

policies.name: National claims review and quality assessment
policies.description: HIRA reviews medical claims, assesses care quality and checks medication use through a national review system.
policies.periodNote: Documented in HIRA’s 2011 institutional report, before the comparison period.

policies.name: Bundled payments for selected procedures
policies.description: Diagnosis-related payments cover seven disease groups, replacing separate charges for each service within those covered admissions.
policies.periodNote: NHIS records compulsory DRG payments for seven groups from 2012; this is not a claim that all care uses bundled payment.

policies.name: Subsidised care plus lifelong insurance
policies.description: Public institutions provide subsidised care. MediShield Life pools the risk of large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatment.
policies.periodNote: MediShield Life began in 2015; this January 2019 ministry statement describes the comparison-period system.

policies.name: Medical savings for remaining bills
policies.description: MediSave balances can pay eligible costs left after subsidies and insurance. These savings are still part of the resources healthcare consumes.
policies.periodNote: Described in the January 2019 ministry statement; savings are not treated as free healthcare in the cost comparison.

policies.name: A fund for patients who cannot afford care
policies.description: MediFund and institutional financial assistance help patients who still face financial difficulty after subsidies, insurance and medical savings.
policies.periodNote: Described in the January 2019 ministry statement.

governmentBudgets.method: For each year, general-government COFOG GF07 total expenditure in national currency / World Bank GDP in current national currency × World Bank GDP per capita in constant 2021 international dollars. Average annual amounts across 2017–2019. OECD currency observations use their UNIT_MULT; IMF CSV observations are already in actual units.
governmentBudgets.scope: Functional public healthcare budgets include capital and medical R&D. They are distinct from the SHA current healthcare total used to rank systems and its financing-source split. Cash/accrual and source revision differences remain visible in source metadata. Missing subgroups are null, not zero.

educationSource.note: 2018 share reaching at least PISA mathematics Level 2: 100 minus low-achiever percentage.

healthcareSource.note: WHO System of Health Accounts current health expenditure, republished by World Bank. Domestic government (including compulsory prepayments and social insurance), domestic private, and external funding partition total current cost. Out-of-pocket payments are included in private cost. Capital formation is excluded; these amounts are not interchangeable with COFOG total government health expenditure.
healthcareSource.conversion: Each annual current-health share of GDP is multiplied by GDP per capita in constant 2021 international dollars; financing-source shares split that annual total before averaging 2017–2019. This uses economy-wide GDP PPP and inflation, not a health-specific price index.
healthcareSource.uncertainty: HALE limits are arithmetic means of WHO annual lower and upper limits, not a new confidence interval for the three-year mean or for policy effects.
